passages: Acid soil. What it looks like. Patches of short, poorly growing plants with weak roots, often with signs of several deficiencies (purple,
yellow) at once.. How to check in the field. Get a soil test (every few years); compare roots of stunted and healthy plants..
How to tell them apart. Whole patches grow badly even with fertilizer; a soil test shows low pH.. When it is likely.
Strongly acid soil can restrict root growth through aluminium or manganese toxicity and nutrient imbalances.
A pH below roughly 5.5 warrants investigation, but effects depend on soil, variety and the test method.
High rainfall and repeated use of acidifying nitrogen fertilizers can increase acidity.. What to do now.
Ask your extension officer to interpret a soil test and advise lime.. Next season.
Use a soil test to plan lime type, amount and timing with your extension officer.
Apply ahead of planting when advised so it has time to react.
A target around pH 6 to 7 is often used for maize; follow the locally recommended target and test method.. Written from.
